text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Some 700 to 1,000 teachers and medical workers picketed parliament to protest against low salaries and insufficient budget funding as parliament debated the 1997 balanced budget.

- The board of the Democratic Party Saimnieks, the largest party in parliament, has nominated the former state minister for investment and credit policy, Sarmite Jegere, as its candidate for finance minister. Prime Minister Andris Shkele commented that the candidature was not ideal.
- Parliament started to consider next year's budget draft at its second and final reading and debated well into the night. The budget debate will continue today and it will probably be passed.
- While considering the budget, parliament decided to double the salary of President Guntis Ulmanis to 1000 lats.
- Despite a moratorium on capital punishment announced by President Ulmanis, the district court of Riga has sentenced a convicted murderer to death.
- Five Latvian pilots held in custody in India went on hunger strike asking for their trial date to be announced as early as possible.
- The cabinet will next week discuss the settlement of the border with Russia as the next round of talks is expected to be held in the first half of December.
